command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Definitions and identities of hyperbolic functions
kcs.statement: Definition of the six hyperbolic functions in terms of exponentials. Graphs and properties of the hyperbolic functions.
kcs.raw: Definition of the six hyperbolic functions in terms of exponentials. Graphs and properties of the hyperbolic functions.
kcs.guidance: For example, $\cosh x = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^x + e^{-x})$, $\operatorname{sech} x = \dfrac{1}{\cosh x} = \dfrac{2}{e^x + e^{-x}}$. Students should be able to derive and use simple identities such as $\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x \equiv 1$ and $\cosh^2 x + \sinh^2 x \equiv \cosh 2x$ and to solve equations such as $a\cosh x + b\sinh x = c$.

kcs.title: Inverse hyperbolic functions and logarithmic forms
kcs.statement: Inverse hyperbolic functions, their graphs, properties and logarithmic equivalents.
kcs.raw: Inverse hyperbolic functions, their graphs, properties and logarithmic equivalents.
kcs.guidance: For example, $\operatorname{arsinh} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{1+x^2}\right)$. Students may be required to prove this and similar results.

kcs.title: Ellipse and hyperbola equations
kcs.statement: Cartesian and parametric equations for the ellipse and hyperbola.
kcs.raw: Cartesian and parametric equations for the ellipse and hyperbola.
kcs.guidance: Extension of work from FP1. Students should be familiar with the equations: $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$; $x = a\cos t, y = b\sin t$. $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$; $x = a\sec t, y = b\tan t$; $x = a\cosh t, y = b\sinh t$.

kcs.title: Focus-directrix properties of ellipse and hyperbola
kcs.statement: The focus-directrix properties of the ellipse and hyperbola, including the eccentricity.
kcs.raw: The focus-directrix properties of the ellipse and hyperbola, including the eccentricity.
kcs.guidance: For example, students should know that, for the ellipse, $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$, the foci are $(ae, 0)$ and $(-ae, 0)$ and the equations of the directrices are $x = \dfrac{a}{e}$ and $x = -\dfrac{a}{e}$.

kcs.title: Tangents and normals to ellipse and hyperbola
kcs.statement: Tangents and normals to these curves.
kcs.raw: Tangents and normals to these curves.
kcs.guidance: The condition for $y = mx + c$ to be a tangent to these curves is expected to be known.

kcs.title: Loci problems with conics
kcs.statement: Simple loci problems.
kcs.raw: Simple loci problems.

kcs.title: Differentiating hyperbolic function expressions
kcs.statement: Differentiation of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.
kcs.raw: Differentiation of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.
kcs.guidance: For example, $\tanh 3x$, $x\sinh^2 x$, $\dfrac{\cosh 2x}{(x+1)^2}$.

kcs.title: Differentiating inverse trig and hyperbolic functions
kcs.statement: Differentiation of inverse functions, including trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
kcs.raw: Differentiation of inverse functions, including trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
kcs.guidance: For example, $\arcsin x + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{artanh}(x^2)$.

kcs.title: Integrating hyperbolic function expressions
kcs.statement: Integration of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.
kcs.raw: Integration of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.

kcs.title: Integrating inverse trig and hyperbolic functions
kcs.statement: Integration of inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
kcs.raw: Integration of inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
kcs.guidance: For example, $\displaystyle\int \operatorname{arsinh} x \, dx$, $\displaystyle\int \arctan x \, dx$.

kcs.title: Hyperbolic and trigonometric substitution integrals
kcs.statement: Integration using hyperbolic and trigonometric substitutions.
kcs.raw: Integration using hyperbolic and trigonometric substitutions.
kcs.guidance: To include the integrals of $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{a^2+x^2}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}$.

kcs.title: Integrals involving quadratic surds
kcs.statement: Use of substitution for integrals involving quadratic surds.
kcs.raw: Use of substitution for integrals involving quadratic surds.
kcs.guidance: In more complicated cases, substitutions will be given.

kcs.title: Deriving reduction formulae for integrals
kcs.statement: The derivation and use of simple reduction formulae.
kcs.raw: The derivation and use of simple reduction formulae.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to derive formulae such as $nI_n = (n-1)I_{n-2}$, $n \geqslant 2$, for $I_n = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^n x \, dx$, and $I_n = I_{n-2} + \dfrac{2\sin((n-1)x)}{n-1}$ for $I_n = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin nx}{\sin x} \, dx$, $n > 0$.

kcs.title: Arc length and surface of revolution
kcs.statement: The calculation of arc length and the area of a surface of revolution.
kcs.raw: The calculation of arc length and the area of a surface of revolution.
kcs.guidance: The equation of the curve may be given in Cartesian or parametric form. Equations in polar form will not be set.

kcs.title: Vector product and triple scalar product
kcs.statement: The vector product $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ and the triple scalar product $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}$.
kcs.raw: The vector product a × b and the triple scalar product a . b × c.
kcs.guidance: The interpretation of $|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}|$ as an area and $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}$ as a volume.

kcs.title: Vector equations of lines and planes
kcs.statement: Use of vectors in problems involving points, lines and planes. The equation of a line in the form $(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{a}) \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$.
kcs.raw: Use of vectors in problems involving points, lines and planes. The equation of a line in the form (r − a) × b = 0.
kcs.guidance: Students may be required to use equivalent Cartesian forms also. Applications to include (i) distance from a point to a plane, (ii) line of intersection of two planes, (iii) shortest distance between two skew lines.

kcs.title: Vector and cartesian equations of planes
kcs.statement: The equation of a plane in the forms $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{n} = p$, $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + s\mathbf{b} + t\mathbf{c}$.
kcs.raw: The equation of a plane in the forms r.n = p, r = a + sb + tc.
kcs.guidance: Students may be required to use equivalent Cartesian forms also.

kcs.title: Matrix transformations in three dimensions
kcs.statement: Linear transformations of column vectors in two and three dimensions and their matrix representation.
kcs.raw: Linear transformations of column vectors in two and three dimensions and their matrix representation.
kcs.guidance: Extension of work from FP1 to 3 dimensions.

kcs.title: Combining 3D matrix transformations
kcs.statement: Combination of transformations. Products of matrices.
kcs.raw: Combination of transformations. Products of matrices.
kcs.guidance: The transformation represented by $AB$ is the transformation represented by $B$ followed by the transformation represented by $A$.

kcs.title: Transpose of a matrix
kcs.statement: Transpose of a matrix.
kcs.raw: Transpose of a matrix.
kcs.guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^T = B^T A^T$.

kcs.title: Evaluating 3x3 determinants
kcs.statement: Evaluation of $3 \times 3$ determinants.
kcs.raw: Evaluation of 3 × 3 determinants.
kcs.guidance: Singular and non-singular matrices.

kcs.title: Inverse of 3x3 matrices
kcs.statement: Inverse of $3 \times 3$ matrices.
kcs.raw: Inverse of 3 × 3 matrices.
kcs.guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

kcs.title: Inverse of 3D transformations
kcs.statement: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.
kcs.raw: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.

kcs.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices
kcs.statement: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $2 \times 2$ and $3 \times 3$ matrices.
kcs.raw: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 matrices.
kcs.guidance: Normalised vectors may be required.

kcs.title: Diagonalising symmetric matrices
kcs.statement: Reduction of symmetric matrices to diagonal form.
kcs.raw: Reduction of symmetric matrices to diagonal form.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to find an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $P^TAP$ is diagonal.
